item.title: MLK used basketball to start a movement. Here's how he built community on the court
item.description: Can basketball really change a nation? Hear from the filmmakers of "Hoops, Hopes & Dreams," to learn how Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. used sports to foster community and connection.

item.title: Fugitive on the run for years is arrested when he turns up at Olympics to watch hockey
item.description: A Slovak fugitive who had been on the run for 16 years was finally arrested when he turned up in Milan to support his national ice hockey team at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics, police said Friday.

item.title: Bay Area shelter cat named one of W Magazine's 'Best Animal Actors of the Year'
item.description: Noochie may be decked out in Prada now, but he is one rags to riches kitty - from his humble beginnings at the Berkeley Humane Society to becoming a Sundance Film Festival darling for his role in "Sorry, Baby."

item.title: 'The Secret Agent' star Wagner Moura making Oscars history: 'Beautiful moment for Brazilian culture'
item.description: Wagner Moura is making Oscars history. "The Secret Agent" star is the first Brazilian nominated for Best Actor. The recognition comes just one year after "I'm Still Here" became Brazil's first film to win Best International Feature at the Academy Awards.

item.title: Trump's Fort Bragg visit spotlights special forces who captured Venezuela's Maduro
item.description: Trump meet with military families and soldiers involved in the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

item.title: SJ Mayor Mahan gaining support, criticism early during CA gubernatorial campaign
item.description: Mahan's campaign reports in just one week, tech billionaires have helped him raise more than $7 million and pay for a Super Bowl ad. San Jose assemblymembers agree that makes him a candidate to watch out for, but not in a good way.

item.title: Deadline looming for Colorado River agreement: Here's how it could affect NorCal
item.description: Seven states that rely on the Colorado River must agree on how to reduce their water intake from a source that is drying out. Some of those states refuse mandatory conservation measures, opting instead for voluntary action. You may not think so, but this will have an impact on Northern California.

item.title: What to know about the Homeland Security shutdown starting this weekend
item.description: Another shutdown for parts of the federal government is expected this weekend as lawmakers debate new restrictions on President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement agenda.

item.title: Judge denies couple's restraining order to keep up Thornton State Beach fence
item.description: This is our first look at Luke Brugnara and Yitong Emily Wen, arguing with the public about the fence they installed to block off the Daly City beach access to the public. "This is actually on- right where that line is, is our property," Brugnara said. "You're actually standing out on our property."

item.title: Tentative $183 million deal reached to end historic San Francisco teachers' strike
item.description: The first San Francisco teachers' strike in 47 years, which has closed schools for days, is ending as SFUSD and the teachers union reached a tentative $183 million deal early Friday morning.
